{{No footnotes|date=November 2024}}
In [[graph theory]], the '''Tutte matrix''' ''A'' of a [[graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] ''G''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(''V'',&nbsp;''E'') is a [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] used to determine the existence of a [[perfect matching]]: that is, a set of [[edge (graph theory)|edge]]s which is incident with each [[vertex (graph theory)|vertex]] exactly once.

If the set of vertices is <math>V = \{1, 2, \dots , n\}</math> then the Tutte matrix is an ''n''-by-''n'' [[skew-symmetric matrix]] ''A'' with entries

: <math>A_{ij} = \begin{cases} x_{ij}\;\;\mbox{if}\;(i,j) \in E \mbox{ and } i<j\\
-x_{ji}\;\;\mbox{if}\;(i,j) \in E \mbox{ and } i>j\\
0\;\;\;\;\mbox{otherwise} \end{cases}</math>

where the ''x''<sub>''ij''</sub> are [[indeterminate (variable)|indeterminate]]s.  The [[determinant]] of this matrix is then a [[polynomial]] (in the variables ''x<sub>ij</sub>'',&nbsp;''i&nbsp;<&nbsp;j'' ): this coincides with the square of the [[Pfaffian]] of the matrix ''A'' and is non-zero (as a polynomial) [[if and only if]] a perfect matching exists.  (This polynomial is not the [[Tutte polynomial]] of ''G''.)

The Tutte matrix is named after [[W. T. Tutte]], and is a generalisation of the [[Edmonds matrix]] for a balanced [[bipartite graph]].
